title: CELL BROADCAST ALERT SYSTEM FOR DISASTER WARNINGS
text:

Ministry of Home Affairs

CELL BROADCAST ALERT SYSTEM FOR DISASTER WARNINGS

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
28 JUL 2026 3:25PM by PIB Delhi

Cell Broadcast Alert System for Disaster Warnings is operated through the Integrated Alert System based on the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) implemented by National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). The system   integrates   five   Warning   Generating   Agencies,  namely the India

Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water Commission (CWC), Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), Defence Geoinformatics Research Establishment (DGRE) and Forest Survey of India (FSI), with the State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs) of all States/UTs. The respective Warning Generating Agencies and SDMAs are responsible for issuing and authorising disaster-specific alerts, while the CAP-based platform facilitates their dissemination through the Cell Broadcast system.

The Cell Broadcast Alert will be used for timely warning to citizens for disaster events with very short lead time like Cyclone, Tsunami, Heavy Rainfall, Lightning, Flash Flood, Thunderstorms, Hailstorm, Avalanche, Cloudburst, Industrial/man-made disasters and other events which merit immediate alerting. The Warning generating agencies provide Geo-targeted warnings and Geo-targeted alerts are disseminated to the public.

Timely receipt of warning and timely dissemination of alerts acts as one of the contributing factor in reducing disaster-related causalities and improving emergency preparedness. The System provides timely alerts to the public, which indirectly improves emergency preparedness and necessary precautions, thus helps in reducing disaster-related casualties.

All warnings generated by the forecasting agencies are translated to the State language of the target population and disseminated to the recipients by the SDMAs. The Alerts are received across all mobile networks and handsets in the geo-targeted area which includes remote and vulnerable areas.

This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.
